candidates.locator: page 5, section part_i, FLOATING SOLIDS, VISIBLE FOAM AND/OR OILS
candidates.exact_span: There shall be no discharge of floating solids or visible foam in other than trace amounts.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a qualitative enforceable limit rather than a numeric one; whether and how reported observations (e.g., presence/absence or severity) are compared depends on interpreting 'trace amounts' and whether this limit is subject to numeric compliance comparison.

candidates.locator: page 5, section part_i, FLOATING SOLIDS, VISIBLE FOAM AND/OR OILS
candidates.exact_span: There shall be no discharge of visible films of oil, globules of oil, grease or solids in or on the water, or coatings on stream banks.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets additional qualitative discharge prohibitions without numeric thresholds; different readings of what constitutes a prohibited 'visible' discharge or coating could change whether a reported observation is treated as exceeding an applicable limit.

candidates.locator: page 5, section part_i, FLOATING SOLIDS, VISIBLE FOAM AND/OR OILS
candidates.exact_span: Samples taken in compliance with the monitoring requirements specified above shall be taken at the discharge after the treatment system and prior to the receiving stream.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies required sampling location and references unspecified 'monitoring requirements specified above'; interpretation of that cross-reference and whether samples were taken at the mandated point can change which limits apply to a measurement (A), whether location-specific monitoring was required (B), and whether absent or off-location data reflects missing required evidence versus a documented no-data state (C).

candidates.locator: page 5, section part_i, B. SCHEDULE OF COMPLIANCE, Delta-BHC Study
candidates.exact_span: The permittee is required to submit a detailed plan to test for Delta-BHC at the source water intake within six months after the effective date of the permit to both EPA and NMED for approval.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Creates a time-bound, approval-conditioned monitoring obligation; whether FY2025 falls inside the six-month planning window or after plan approval affects whether delta-BHC monitoring was required and how to classify periods before plan submission or approval.

candidates.locator: page 5, section part_i, B. SCHEDULE OF COMPLIANCE, Delta-BHC Study
candidates.exact_span: Once approved, the permittee must collect and analyze samples for delta-BHC at least once a quarter or more frequent during the 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th year of the permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Monitoring frequency and applicability hinge on permit year and prior approval; mapping Federal FY2025 to the permit's 2nd–5th years and interpreting 'at least once a quarter or more frequent' changes which quarters require sampling and whether missing delta-BHC results indicate unmet obligations or conditional non-requirement.

candidates.locator: page 5, section part_i, B. SCHEDULE OF COMPLIANCE, Delta-BHC Study
candidates.exact_span: The results of this study shall be attached to the DMR reports to EPA.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Ties delta-BHC study results to DMR reporting; interpretation of whether results were due on DMRs during applicable years affects whether monitoring/reporting was required and how to classify DMRs lacking attached study results.

candidates.locator: page 5, section part_i, C. MONITORING AND REPORTING (MINOR DISCHARGERS), item 1
candidates.exact_span: Discharge Monitoring Report Form(s) shall be submitted quarterly. Each quarterly submittal shall include separate forms for each month of the reporting period.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines quarterly DMR submission with separate monthly forms; interpretation of which months within FY2025 require reported results versus documented no-data affects monitoring-obligation evaluation and missing-evidence classification for months without ordinary numeric results.

candidates.locator: page 5, section part_i, C. MONITORING AND REPORTING (MINOR DISCHARGERS), item 2
candidates.exact_span: Reporting periods shall end on the last day of the months March, June, September, and December.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Fixes quarterly reporting-period boundaries; different alignment of permit reporting periods with Federal FY2025 months changes which measurement/limit pairs fall in each evaluated period and which monitoring expectations apply to each quarter.

candidates.locator: page 5, section part_i, C. MONITORING AND REPORTING (MINOR DISCHARGERS), item 3
candidates.exact_span: The first Discharge Monitoring Report(s) shall represent facility operations from the effective date of the permit through the last day of the current reporting period.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines the initial reporting window spanning partial months from permit effective date; interpretation of how operations in that transitional period map to monthly DMR expectations affects whether monitoring was required and how to treat partial-period missing or non-numeric results.
